regulatory_applicability.match_result: No match on any entry. This application is a standalone single-developer academic Windows desktop application managing student academic records for three computing degree programmes (BCA, MCA, IIMCA). It has no aviation domain concept whatsoever: no airman, certificate, rating, medical, endorsement, aircraft, registration, designee or examiner entity exists in its one 10-column table or anywhere in its 461 lines of hand-written code.
regulatory_applicability.consequence: Every rule in this catalog is a business convention, a defect or an implementation artifact, not a regulatory requirement. regulatory_traceability is therefore omitted from every rule rather than populated with a fabricated citation or a blanket not_applicable stub, and no BR-MISSING-NNN records were generated, because a regulation this application does not implement cannot have gaps in it.
regulatory_applicability.discrepancy_finding: The governing profile declared for this dispatch (faa) does not plausibly govern this application's domain. The Pass 0 catalog classifies its business_domain as 'Admin' and describes it as a single-developer academic or portfolio project; no input artifact asserts a different profile, so the declared profile stands as authoritative per the dispatch rules and was used as the sole source of policy. The mismatch is recorded here for the profile owner: either this application is mis-assigned to the faa profile, or faa's regulatory_sources need an entry covering non-aviation administrative systems. Note also that the Part 47 applicable_systems list in profiles/faa/compliance.yaml still carries an unresolved TODO(human) marker, so that list is self-described as unconfirmed.

form1-dashboard.role: Startup shell, navigation host and statistics dashboard
form1-dashboard.notes: All twelve reported statistics are computed here from twelve independent COUNT queries with no GROUP BY. Five of them are invalidated by a hardcoded current year of 2023 (BR-072) and the gender and course breakdowns silently undercount (BR-070, BR-071). Also owns the panel-reparenting navigation that is the most complex single behaviour in the application (BR-078).

insert-form.notes: Parameterized insert of ten columns with no explicit validation whatsoever. The three categorical fields are mandatory only because an unselected dropdown throws (BR-011), and that accidental guard is then defeated from the second insert onward because the clear routine cannot clear a DropDownList combo (BR-020). Carries the mobile-number 32-bit ceiling (BR-017).

edit-form.notes: Roll number is immutable here (BR-031) — the system's clearest invariant. The load path is entirely unguarded and runs in the constructor (BR-035), and records whose stored categorical values fall outside the hardcoded dropdown lists are permanently un-editable and can be silently overwritten (BR-033).

view-form.role: Read, search and delete path; launches the edit form
view-form.notes: Highest rule density. Contains the application's only unparameterized SQL (BR-052), its only confirmation dialog (BR-056), its only physical delete (BR-057), and the connection close that breaks the dashboard afterwards (BR-004). Search covers only two of ten fields (BR-054).

module1-db-connection.notes: One shared global connection reached by a hardcoded absolute developer path (BR-002), so the committed database is not the one the application opens. Also the anchor for the system-wide absences: no transactions (BR-093), no audit or provenance (BR-095), and schema-only field-length rules (BR-096).

my-project-infrastructure.role: Application framework configuration and compiler options
my-project-infrastructure.notes: Holds four rules that exist only as build and framework settings yet govern behaviour everywhere: no authentication or authorization at all (BR-090), Option Strict Off as the enabling precondition for five runtime-only failure modes (BR-091), case-sensitivity divergence from the database engine (BR-092), and concurrent instances with last-write-wins (BR-094).

rules.name: Lazy single global database connection
rules.description: The application opens exactly one shared OleDbConnection, held in a module-level Public variable, and opens it only when its State is Closed. Every form calls Module1.connectDB() defensively before issuing SQL, so the first caller opens the connection and all later callers no-op. This is the whole of the application's connection management: there is no pool, no per-operation connection, no using/dispose block and no close on exit.
rules.complexity_rationale: Two branches (open/already-open) in a 5-line procedure, but the consequences are application-wide because every data operation depends on this one object.

There is no configuration file entry, no App.config setting, no relative path and no environment override — App.config contains only a supportedRuntime element. rules.name: One shared connection serves all forms concurrently
rules.description: dbcon is a Public module-level variable, so the dashboard, insert, edit and view forms all issue commands against the same physical connection object. Because child forms are hosted simultaneously inside Panel5 and are only hidden rather than disposed, two forms can hold live readers or adapters against this one connection. OleDb permits only one open DataReader per connection, so an unclosed reader blocks every other operation.
rules.complexity_rationale: No branching, but it creates implicit cross-module temporal coupling between four form modules that are otherwise independent.

rules.name: Delete closes the shared connection, breaking later dashboard refresh

rules.description: The create path inserts exactly one row into the students table with all ten columns supplied from the entry form: rollno, fname, lname, fathername, mobno, altmobno, gender, course, yoa and dob. rules.name: Gender, course and session are mandatory only by accident
rules.description: No explicit required-field validation exists anywhere in the create path. However the three dropdowns are read via SelectedItem.ToString(), and none of them has a default SelectedIndex, so they start unselected and SelectedItem is Nothing. With OptionStrict Off the call compiles and fails at runtime with NullReferenceException, caught by the method's blanket Catch and reported as 'Error: Object reference not set to an instance of an object.'. The three dropdowns are therefore de-facto mandatory, enforced by an exception rather than by validation, and the user is told nothing about which field is missing. The seven text fields remain genuinely optional.
rules.complexity_rationale: The rule is emergent from the interaction of three separate facts — no SelectedIndex default in the Designer, SelectedItem.ToString() in the handler, and a blanket Catch — none of which states a validation intent.

rules.name: Date of birth is persisted from a culture-formatted display string
rules.description: Both the create and the update path bind the date of birth as dtpDOB.Text — the DateTimePicker's locale-formatted display string — rather than dtpDOB.Value, its typed DateTime. The value is written into a DATE/TIME column, so the OLEDB provider must parse the display string back into a date using the current workstation's culture. On a machine whose short-date order differs from the one that wrote the row, 03/04/2005 is read as 3 April or 4 March depending only on regional settings, and the application has no way to tell which was meant.
rules.complexity_rationale: A one-token difference (.Text instead of .Value) whose effect is a silent, locale-dependent data corruption spanning the insert path, the update path and the DATE/TIME column.

rules.name: Mobile numbers cannot exceed 2,147,483,647
rules.description: MobNo and AltMobNo are declared in the Access table definition as 32-bit Long Integer columns, four bytes each, confirmed by decoding the table-definition page of studentDB.accdb directly. The entry form collects them as unconstrained free text with no MaxLength and no numeric validation. Any mobile number at or above 2,147,483,648 therefore cannot be stored — which excludes every ten-digit Indian mobile number, all of which begin with 6, 7, 8 or 9. The failure appears as a raw provider message in a message box and no row is created. Storing phone numbers as integers also silently discards leading zeros, country prefixes, spaces and '+' signs.
rules.complexity_rationale: The constraint is invisible in the application source entirely — it exists only in the binary column definition — and it contradicts the form's own free-text input affordance.

rules.name: Named parameters bind positionally, not by name
rules.description: The OLEDB provider does not support named parameters: the '@Name' tokens in the SQL text are treated as anonymous placeholders and parameters are bound strictly in the order they were added to the collection. The insert and update statements currently work only because the AddWithValue calls happen to appear in the same order as the placeholders. The names are decorative, so any future reordering of either the SQL column list or the AddWithValue block silently shifts every value one column sideways rather than raising an error.
rules.complexity_rationale: A latent provider-level semantic that is contradicted by the source's own appearance of name-based binding; correctness depends on a textual ordering coincidence maintained in two separate statements.

rules.name: Post-insert refresh targets VB default instances, not the visible forms
rules.description: After a successful insert the handler calls Form1.LoadData() and ViewForm.LoadData() using VB.NET's My.Forms default-instance feature, where a form type name resolves to an implicit per-thread singleton. Form1.LoadData() happens to work, because Form1 is the application's MainForm and so the default instance IS the visible dashboard. ViewForm.LoadData() does not: the visible grid was created explicitly with New ViewForm() and reparented into Panel5, so the default-instance call constructs or reuses a second, invisible ViewForm, runs its Load handler, and refreshes a grid nobody can see. The visible grid is left stale. The user's grid only catches up later, by the unrelated route of closing an edit form or re-clicking View.
rules.complexity_rationale: Correctness depends on an invisible language feature that silently resolves two syntactically identical calls to two different objects, and the behaviour spans three modules — insert-form, form1-dashboard and view-form.

rules.name: Field reset fails to clear the three dropdowns
rules.description: ClearFields resets the six text boxes and the date picker, then attempts to clear the three dropdowns by assigning an empty string to their Text property. Because all three combos are DropDownStyle = DropDownList, the Text property only accepts values present in the Items collection, so assigning an empty string is ignored and the previous selection remains displayed and selected. The consequence is a real data-integrity rule: after the first successful insert of a session, every subsequent record silently inherits the previous record's gender, course and year of admission unless the user notices and changes them. Clearing would require SelectedIndex = -1.
rules.complexity_rationale: Emergent from a WinForms property semantic that contradicts the code's evident intent; it also masks BR-011, converting a loud failure into silent wrong data.

rules.name: Default date of birth is today
rules.description: The DateTimePicker has no Value, MinDate, MaxDate or Format set in the Designer, so it initialises to the current date and accepts the control's full default range of 1753-01-01 to 9998-12-31. ClearFields explicitly re-sets it to Date.Now. A user who does not touch the control therefore submits today's date as the student's date of birth — a plausible-looking value that is always wrong. No plausibility check exists: future birth dates and eighteenth-century birth dates are both accepted.

rules.name: All create failures are reported as raw exception text and lost
rules.description: The entire create path is wrapped in a single Try/Catch that catches Exception and displays 'Error: ' concatenated with the raw .NET message. There is no logging, no telemetry, no error code, no field attribution, no retry and no transaction to roll back. Duplicate-key violations, mobile-number overflows, provider failures, missing-dropdown null references and connection faults are all presented identically, so the user cannot distinguish a data-entry mistake from an infrastructure outage, and no record of the failure survives the dismissal of the message box.
rules.complexity_rationale: One catch block, but it is the sole error-handling mechanism on the create path and it erases the diagnostic distinction between every failure mode in the system.

rules.name: Roll number is the user-supplied record key, unique by database index only
rules.description: Roll number is the system's sole record identifier: every single-row read, update and delete matches on it, and the grid reads it back by column name to drive those operations. It is typed freely by the user on the insert form with no format mask, no length limit, no check-digit and no generation scheme. Uniqueness is enforced solely by the PrimaryKey index present in the Access table definition, confirmed by direct decode of studentDB.accdb; the application performs no duplicate pre-check, so a collision surfaces only as an untriaged provider error from BR-022. Note that the two Pass-1 inputs disagreed on whether this index exists, and the disagreement was resolved against the binary in favour of its existence.
rules.complexity_rationale: Conceptually simple but load-bearing for four separate code paths, and its one enforcement mechanism lives outside the application source entirely.

rules.name: Load one student for editing by roll number
rules.description: The edit form is constructed with a roll number, runs a parameterized SELECT * for that key, and if a row is returned populates the ten controls from it. The read happens in the constructor, before the form is shown. The reader is closed unconditionally after the single Read attempt; only the first matching row is ever consumed.
rules.complexity_rationale: Single parameterized read with one conditional populate; the complexity lives in its failure modes rather than its logic.

conditions.condition: An EditForm is constructed with a roll number, or UpdateRollNo is called on an existing instance
A row with that roll number exists

actions.action: Populate the six text boxes, three dropdowns and the date picker from the row
Close the reader

test_hints.happy_path: Select a row in the grid, click Update, confirm all ten fields are pre-filled from the database.
error_paths: DateTime.Parse of an empty or unparseable date of birth throws inside the constructor (BR-034, BR-035)
A value outside the hardcoded dropdown lists leaves that control blank (BR-033)
boundary_conditions: No matching row leaves every control at its designer default with no message (BR-036)
If duplicate roll numbers somehow exist, only the first is loaded while the update writes to all of them (BR-037)

rules.name: Roll number is immutable after creation
rules.description: On the edit form the roll-number text box is set ReadOnly in the Designer, and the UPDATE statement lists only the nine other columns in its SET clause while using rollno exclusively in the WHERE clause. Re-keying a student is therefore impossible through the application: the only route is delete-and-recreate, which loses the record entirely in between because there is no transaction and no audit trail. The control is ReadOnly rather than disabled, so it remains tab-reachable and its value still posts.
rules.complexity_rationale: Enforced by one Designer property plus the shape of one SQL statement; simple, but it is the system's strongest and clearest invariant.

conditions.condition: The edit form is displayed for an existing record

actions.action: txtRollNo is ReadOnly so the key cannot be retyped
The UPDATE SET clause omits rollno and the WHERE clause binds the original key
The in-memory rollno field, not the text box, supplies the WHERE value

test_hints.happy_path: Open a record for editing and confirm the roll number is displayed but cannot be typed into.
error_paths: No application path can change a roll number
boundary_conditions: Contrast the insert form, where the same control is freely editable — the field's mutability is context-dependent and defined in two different Designer files
Correcting a mistyped roll number requires delete plus re-entry with no atomicity

rules.name: Update rewrites all nine mutable fields unconditionally
rules.description: Saving an edit issues a single UPDATE that writes all nine non-key columns from the current control values, regardless of whether the user changed any of them. There is no dirty-field tracking, no optimistic concurrency token, no row-version check and no comparison against the loaded values. Any value that failed to populate correctly on load — most importantly a dropdown left blank because its stored value is outside the hardcoded list — is therefore written back as the new truth, so merely opening and saving a record can destroy data the user never touched.
rules.complexity_rationale: Linear statement, but combined with BR-033's silent load failure it converts a read-only glance into a destructive write, and it is the system's only concurrency semantic.

conditions.condition: User clicks Update on the edit form

actions.action: Write all nine mutable columns from current control state, keyed on the original roll number
Show 'Record updated successfully', refresh the dashboard and close the form

test_hints.happy_path: Change a last name, save, confirm only the intended visible change is observable.
error_paths: Any dropdown left blank by BR-033 raises NullReferenceException at SelectedItem.ToString() and the update is abandoned
Mobile number above the 32-bit ceiling fails the same way as on insert (BR-017)
boundary_conditions: Two concurrent application instances editing the same record — the second save wins with no detection (BR-094)
Opening and immediately saving a record rewrites every field, updating nothing visibly but defeating any external change made in between

rules.name: Records holding out-of-list values cannot be edited
rules.description: Load populates the three dropdowns by assigning the stored string to SelectedItem. For a DropDownList combo this performs an exact, case-sensitive lookup in the hardcoded Items collection; a value not found is silently ignored and the control is left with no selection. Save then reads SelectedItem.ToString(), which throws NullReferenceException. The practical rule is that any record whose gender, course or year of admission lies outside the hardcoded lists — a 2024 intake, a decommissioned programme, or a value differing only in letter case — is permanently un-editable through the application, and the failure is reported only as a generic object-reference error.
rules.complexity_rationale: Emergent from four independent facts — DropDownList lookup semantics, case-sensitive matching, the hardcoded Designer lists, and the unconditional SelectedItem.ToString() on save — none of which is visible from the others, and it spans the edit module, both Designer files and the data itself.

conditions.condition: A stored gender, course or yoa value is absent from the Designer Items list, including by case difference
The user then clicks Update

actions.action: SelectedItem assignment silently fails and the combo shows no selection
SelectedItem.ToString() throws NullReferenceException and the update is abandoned
The blanket Catch reports a generic object-reference error

test_hints.happy_path: A record whose three categorical values are all in the hardcoded lists loads and saves normally.
error_paths: A record with yoa '2024' cannot be saved — generic NullReferenceException
A record with gender 'male' in lower case fails the same way despite being semantically valid
A record with a retired course code is locked out of all editing
boundary_conditions: Because the expired year list (BR-015) already excludes current intakes, this rule will capture every future record created by any other means
If the user manually selects a valid value in the blanked combo, BR-032 overwrites the original stored value with it, silently destroying the out-of-list datum

rules.name: Date of birth is re-parsed from text with no culture specified
rules.description: Load reads the stored date of birth, converts it to a string with ToString(), and parses it back with DateTime.Parse — both using the ambient culture — before assigning it to the date picker, whose Value setter also enforces the control's MinDate/MaxDate range. Combined with BR-016's culture-formatted write, a date of birth makes two unanchored culture round-trips per edit cycle. An unparseable or empty stored value throws FormatException, and a value outside the picker's range throws ArgumentOutOfRangeException, in both cases from inside the constructor.
rules.complexity_rationale: A two-stage culture-sensitive conversion with three distinct exception modes, executed in a constructor with no handling, and coupled to the matching defect on the write side in a different module.

conditions.condition: A record is loaded for editing
The stored date of birth is empty, null, unparseable under the current culture, or outside the picker range

actions.action: DateTime.Parse under the ambient culture converts the string back to a date, with day/month ambiguity unresolved
FormatException or ArgumentOutOfRangeException is raised inside the constructor and escapes to the caller

test_hints.happy_path: A date written and read on the same machine under one locale round-trips intact.
error_paths: NULL or empty date of birth — FormatException escapes the constructor and crashes from ViewForm.btnUpdate_Click, which has no handler
Date written under a day-first locale and read under a month-first locale — silently transposed for day values 1-12
boundary_conditions: The exception occurs after the reader is opened but before stReader.Close(), so it also leaks the reader and poisons the shared connection (BR-003, BR-035)
Dates before 1753-01-01 are storable in Access but outside the picker's range

rules.name: Unguarded database I/O in the edit form constructor
rules.description: The edit form performs its database read from inside its constructor, with no Try/Catch, and the constructor is invoked from ViewForm's Update handler, which also has no Try/Catch. Every failure mode of the load path — provider error, closed connection, parse failure, picker range violation — therefore propagates as an unhandled exception and terminates the application, in contrast to the save path which is fully wrapped. The failure also occurs between opening the reader and closing it, leaving the shared connection with an open reader.
rules.complexity_rationale: The asymmetry between a fully guarded save path and a completely unguarded load path spans two modules and is only visible by reading both together.

conditions.condition: EditForm is constructed and LoadData raises any exception

actions.action: The exception escapes the constructor into ViewForm.btnUpdate_Click, which does not handle it, and the application terminates
stReader.Close() is skipped, leaving an open reader on the shared global connection

test_hints.happy_path: A well-formed record loads without incident.
error_paths: Record with a null date of birth — unhandled crash rather than a message box
Connection left closed by a prior delete (BR-004) — unhandled crash on opening any record for edit
boundary_conditions: The reuse path UpdateRollNo calls the same unguarded LoadData from a normal method, where the exception escapes into btnUpdate_Click identically
No Using block or Finally exists anywhere in the file, so reader cleanup depends entirely on the happy path

rules.name: A missing record silently yields a blank edit form
rules.description: The load path guards its populate block with If stReader.Read(), but supplies no Else branch. When no row matches the roll number the method closes the reader and returns, leaving every control at its Designer default: empty text boxes, unselected dropdowns and today's date. The user is shown what looks like an edit form for the selected student with no indication that nothing was loaded. Clicking Update then raises NullReferenceException from the unselected dropdowns, so the condition is reported only as a generic error.
rules.complexity_rationale: A missing Else branch whose consequence is a misleading UI state rather than an error, and whose eventual symptom appears in a different method and is indistinguishable from BR-011 and BR-033.

conditions.condition: No row matches the roll number passed to the edit form

actions.action: Skip the populate block, close the reader, return with no message
Present a blank form that appears to be editing the selected record

test_hints.happy_path: A matching row exists and the form is populated.
error_paths: Record deleted by a concurrent instance between grid load and edit click — blank form, then a generic object-reference error on save
boundary_conditions: Selecting the grid's phantom new-row placeholder yields a Nothing roll number (BR-060), which reaches here as a non-matching key
If the user fills the blank form in and saves, the UPDATE matches no rows and still reports 'Record updated successfully' because ExecuteNonQuery's zero row count is never checked

rules.name: Update and delete affect every row sharing the roll number
rules.description: Both the UPDATE and the DELETE are keyed on rollno with no row limit. The PrimaryKey index normally guarantees one match, so the rule is latent rather than active today, but it is the system's only statement about cardinality: if the index were ever absent — as one Pass-1 input incorrectly reported — or if data were loaded by another tool, a single Update or Delete action would silently modify or remove every matching record while reporting success.
rules.complexity_rationale: Simple unbounded WHERE clause; low logic, but it is the point where the integrity of the whole key assumption is cashed in.

conditions.condition: More than one row shares a roll number

actions.action: UPDATE rewrites all matching rows
DELETE removes all matching rows
The returned row count is discarded, so success is reported regardless of how many rows were affected

test_hints.happy_path: Exactly one row matches and exactly one row is affected.
error_paths: Zero rows match — ExecuteNonQuery returns 0 and success is still reported (see BR-036)
boundary_conditions: Access text matching is case-insensitive on read, so roll numbers differing only in case would both match a single WHERE while the case-sensitive index treats them as distinct keys — the one configuration in which this rule becomes active

rules.name: Post-update refresh is indirect and partial
rules.description: A successful update refreshes the dashboard via the Form1 default instance and then closes the edit form. The grid is not refreshed directly; it updates only because ViewForm attached a FormClosed handler when it launched the edit form, and that handler reloads the grid. The refresh of the user's primary view therefore depends on an event subscription made in a different module, which is why the update path happens to work where the insert path (BR-019) does not.
rules.complexity_rationale: Two statements, but the cascade's correctness rests on an event handler registered elsewhere, making the dependency invisible from this file.

conditions.condition: An update succeeds

actions.action: Refresh dashboard statistics through the Form1 default instance
Close the edit form, firing ViewForm's FormClosed handler which reloads the grid

test_hints.happy_path: Edit a record, save, and observe both the grid row and the dashboard counts updated.
error_paths: If the connection was closed by a prior delete (BR-004), Form1.LoadData throws and the blanket Catch reports a save error even though the update committed
boundary_conditions: Closing the edit form via Cancel also triggers the grid reload, so a cancelled edit still causes a database round trip
Repeated launches re-register the handler (BR-062), so the grid reloads once per launch accumulated so far

rules.name: List every student, unordered and unpaged
rules.description: The default grid population binds the entire students table via SELECT * with no WHERE, no ORDER BY, no TOP and no paging. Display order is therefore whatever physical order the Access engine returns, which is not guaranteed stable across inserts and deletes, and the grid grows without bound as the table grows. This is the application's only record-listing mechanism.
rules.complexity_rationale: One statement and one data binding, but it is the sole read surface and carries the system's entire display-ordering semantics by omission.

conditions.condition: The view form loads, or a refresh is triggered after an insert, update or delete

actions.action: Fill a fresh DataSet from SELECT * FROM students and bind it to the grid

test_hints.happy_path: Open the View panel and see all student rows in the grid.
error_paths: Provider or file error during Fill raises an unhandled exception — neither LoadData nor ViewForm_Load has a Try/Catch
boundary_conditions: Empty table yields an empty grid plus the phantom new-row placeholder (BR-060)
Every refresh creates a new DataSet and discards the old one without disposing it
Row order can change between refreshes, so a user's visual position is not stable

rules.name: Search matches exact roll number or partial first name
rules.description: The search applies a single OR predicate: rollno equal to the search term, or fname containing the term as a substring. Roll number matching is exact and whole-value while first-name matching is a leading-and-trailing wildcard LIKE, so the two halves of one input box behave under different rules. Access text comparison is case-insensitive, so both halves ignore letter case regardless of the application's own case-sensitive string settings.
rules.complexity_rationale: A two-branch predicate with asymmetric matching semantics across a single user input, plus an engine-level case-sensitivity behaviour that differs from the host language's.

conditions.condition: User clicks Search with a non-blank term

actions.action: Append WHERE rollno = '<term>' OR fname LIKE '%<term>%' and rebind the grid
Trim leading and trailing whitespace from the term before use

test_hints.happy_path: Search a known roll number and get exactly that student; search a name fragment and get all students whose first name contains it.
error_paths: A term containing a single quote breaks the SQL and raises an unhandled syntax error (BR-052)
boundary_conditions: A numeric term can match both a roll number and a first-name substring, returning a union
Whitespace-only input is trimmed to empty and returns everything (BR-053)
Access treats both the equality and the LIKE as case-insensitive, unlike the application's Binary comparison setting (BR-092)

rules.name: Search term is concatenated directly into SQL
rules.description: The search predicate is built by string concatenation of the raw user input into the SQL text, with no parameterization and no quote escaping — the only place in the application where this happens, since the insert, update, delete and single-row read paths are all parameterized. The input box has no MaxLength. Any apostrophe terminates the literal and alters the statement, so an operator can read or modify arbitrary table content, and because the grid displays whatever the altered statement returns, the injection has a direct output channel. Access's ACE engine does not support stacked statements, which limits but does not eliminate the exposure.
rules.complexity_rationale: A single concatenation, but it is the application's one unparameterized data path and it both reads and displays attacker-controlled query results.

conditions.condition: A search term containing SQL metacharacters is submitted

actions.action: Concatenate the raw term into the WHERE clause without escaping or parameterization
Execute the resulting statement and display its result set in the grid

test_hints.happy_path: An ordinary alphanumeric term produces well-formed SQL.
error_paths: Term containing one apostrophe, for example O'Brien — unhandled syntax error crashes the application, so legitimate names are also affected
Term crafted as a closing quote plus OR 1=1 returns the entire table irrespective of the intended filter
boundary_conditions: A legitimate Irish or Italian surname in the first-name field is indistinguishable from an injection attempt
LIKE wildcards % _ and the Access-specific * ? in user input silently change the match semantics
No handler wraps LoadSData, so every malformed statement terminates the process

rules.name: Blank search returns the entire table
rules.description: If the trimmed search term is null, empty or whitespace, the WHERE clause is omitted entirely and the query degenerates to SELECT * FROM students. Clearing the box and pressing Search is therefore the application's only explicit way to clear an active filter and return to the full list; there is no separate reset control.
rules.complexity_rationale: One guard clause with one branch.

conditions.condition: The trimmed search term is empty or whitespace

actions.action: Skip the WHERE clause and bind all rows

test_hints.happy_path: Clear the search box, click Search, and the full list returns.
error_paths: No failure mode — the guard clause always succeeds; the risk is the silent filter reset described under boundary conditions
boundary_conditions: A term of only spaces is trimmed to empty and returns everything rather than matching nothing

An active filter also silently resets whenever any refresh path calls LoadData instead of LoadSData — after a delete, after closing an edit form, or on reload — so the user's filter is discarded without notice

rules.name: Search ignores seven of the ten stored fields
rules.description: Only roll number and first name participate in search. Last name, father's name, both mobile numbers, gender, course, year of admission and date of birth are all unsearchable, so a user who knows only a student's surname or phone number cannot locate the record except by scrolling the unordered full list. There is no filter-by-course or filter-by-year capability anywhere in the application despite those being the dashboard's primary reporting axes.
rules.complexity_rationale: Defined by what the predicate omits rather than by any branching.

conditions.condition: A user searches by any attribute other than roll number or first name

actions.action: No rows match and the grid appears empty, with no message explaining that the field is not searchable

test_hints.happy_path: Search by first name or roll number succeeds.
error_paths: Search by surname returns an empty grid that is indistinguishable from 'no such student'
boundary_conditions: A surname that also happens to be someone's first name returns a confusing partial result
The dashboard breaks students down by gender, course and year, none of which can be used as a filter in the only list view

rules.name: Mutation requires an explicit grid row selection
rules.description: Both Update and Delete begin by testing SelectedRows.Count > 0 and refuse to proceed with a message box if nothing is selected. Combined with the grid's FullRowSelect mode, the unit of operation is always a whole student record, and the roll number is read back out of the selected row's rollno cell to key the operation. This selection test is the closest thing the application has to an authorization check.
rules.complexity_rationale: A single guard duplicated across two handlers; simple, but it is the only gate in front of a destructive operation.

conditions.condition: User clicks Update or Delete
No grid row is selected

actions.action: Show 'Please select a row to edit' or 'Please select a row to delete' and abandon the operation
Otherwise read the roll number from the selected row's rollno cell

test_hints.happy_path: Select a row, click Delete, confirm, and the record is removed.
error_paths: Click Delete with nothing selected — advisory message, no action
boundary_conditions: Clicking any single cell selects the whole row, so partial selection cannot occur
Selecting the phantom new-row placeholder passes the count test but yields a Nothing roll number and crashes (BR-060)

rules.name: Deletion requires explicit Yes/No confirmation
rules.description: Deletion is the only operation in the application guarded by a confirmation dialog: a Yes/No message box asking 'Are you sure you want to delete this record?'. Only an affirmative answer proceeds. No other destructive or semi-destructive action — update, which rewrites all nine fields, or application exit, which discards unsaved entry data — asks for confirmation.
rules.complexity_rationale: One conditional on a dialog result; the significance is that it is the system's only confirmation gate.

conditions.condition: A row is selected and Delete is clicked
The user answers Yes

actions.action: Execute the parameterized DELETE for that roll number
On No, abandon silently with the record intact

test_hints.happy_path: Answer Yes and the record is deleted; answer No and nothing changes.
error_paths: Provider failure during the delete raises an unhandled exception — the delete handler has no Try/Catch, unlike insert and update
boundary_conditions: The dialog names no student, so it cannot be used to verify that the correct record is about to be destroyed
Answering Yes is irreversible — there is no undo, no soft delete and no audit record (BR-057)

rules.name: Deletion is physical and unrecoverable
rules.description: Deletion issues a hard DELETE against the sole table. There is no status or is_deleted column, no archive table, no soft-delete flag, no retention period and no audit record of who deleted what or when; the schema has no created, modified or deleted timestamp columns at all. Once confirmed, the student record and every attribute of it — including the personal data of the student and of the named parent — is irrecoverable from the application. Pass-1 forensics recovered six previously deleted rows from page slack in the database file, which is a data-remanence consideration rather than an application-level recovery route.
rules.complexity_rationale: One statement, but it defines the record lifecycle's terminal state and the complete absence of auditability.

conditions.condition: A delete is confirmed

actions.action: Physically remove the row with DELETE FROM students WHERE rollno = ?
Report success and reload the grid; no audit record is written anywhere

test_hints.happy_path: Confirmed delete removes exactly one row.
error_paths: Zero rows matched still reports 'Record deleted successfully' because the ExecuteNonQuery row count is discarded
boundary_conditions: No transaction wraps the delete, so there is nothing to roll back
Deleted personal data remains recoverable from the Access file's free pages, which is a disposal concern rather than a feature

rules.name: Deletion does not refresh the dashboard
rules.description: The delete path reloads the grid but never calls the dashboard refresh, unlike the insert and update paths which both do. After deleting a student the dashboard's gender, course and year counts remain at their pre-delete values until the user navigates Home — and because the delete also closed the shared connection (BR-004), that navigation raises an unhandled exception instead. The three mutation paths therefore have three different and mutually inconsistent refresh behaviours.
rules.complexity_rationale: Defined by a missing call; its significance is the inconsistency across the three mutation paths and its interaction with the connection-close defect.

conditions.condition: A delete completes successfully

actions.action: Reload the grid only; no dashboard refresh is invoked
Dashboard statistics remain stale and overstate the student population

test_hints.happy_path: Delete a record, then navigate Home on a run where no delete-induced connection close interferes, and the counts correct themselves.
error_paths: Delete then click Dashboard — unhandled InvalidOperationException from the closed connection (BR-004)
boundary_conditions: A user who deletes several records and then reads the dashboard without navigating sees counts that are silently too high
Insert refreshes the dashboard but not the visible grid; delete refreshes the visible grid but not the dashboard; update refreshes both — no two paths agree

rules.name: Only one record may be acted on at a time
rules.description: The grid sets MultiSelect = False and SelectionMode = FullRowSelect, so exactly one complete student record can be selected. Bulk update and bulk delete are structurally impossible, and there is no select-all, no checkbox column and no batch operation anywhere in the application. Every mutation is a single-record, single-statement, interactive action.
rules.complexity_rationale: Two Designer properties that together fix the cardinality of every mutation in the system.

conditions.condition: A user interacts with the grid selection

actions.action: Selecting a row clears any previous selection; at most one row is ever selected
Clicking any cell selects the entire row

test_hints.happy_path: Click a row; the whole row highlights and the previous selection clears.
error_paths: No failure mode — the constraint is enforced by the framework and cannot be violated from the UI
boundary_conditions: Ctrl-click and Shift-click cannot extend the selection
Code that reads SelectedRows(0) is therefore always safe with respect to index bounds once the count test passes

rules.name: Grid is read-only yet exposes a phantom addable row
rules.description: The grid is explicitly ReadOnly, so in-place cell editing is impossible and all mutation must route through the Update and Delete buttons. However AllowUserToAddRows and AllowUserToDeleteRows are never set and so retain their permissive True defaults: a phantom new-row placeholder is rendered at the bottom of the grid, and the Delete key can remove rows from the bound DataTable without touching the database. ReadOnly does not suppress either behaviour. Selecting the placeholder passes the selection test in BR-055 and then yields a Nothing roll-number cell, so Cells("rollno").Value.ToString() raises NullReferenceException in both the Update and the Delete handler, neither of which has any exception handling.
rules.complexity_rationale: Three interacting grid properties, two of them unset and therefore invisible in source, producing a reachable crash path and a false visual row count.

conditions.condition: The grid is displayed with AllowUserToAddRows at its default True
The user selects the trailing placeholder row and clicks Update or Delete

actions.action: Cells('rollno').Value is Nothing and ToString() raises NullReferenceException, terminating the application
Pressing Delete on a real row removes it from the bound DataTable only, so the grid and the database silently disagree until the next reload

test_hints.happy_path: Operate only on real data rows and the placeholder is merely cosmetic.
error_paths: Select the trailing empty row and click Delete — unhandled NullReferenceException
Select the trailing empty row and click Update — same crash, from the EditForm construction path
boundary_conditions: An empty students table still shows one row, so the grid never looks genuinely empty
Any row-count logic over the grid is off by one
Pressing the Delete key appears to delete a record but does not persist, and the row returns on the next refresh

rules.name: Grid shape is dictated entirely by SELECT *
rules.description: No columns are defined in the Designer: AutoGenerateColumns is enabled at runtime and AutoSizeColumnsMode is set to Fill, so the grid's column count, order and header text all come from the result set of SELECT *. Users therefore see raw database column names — rollno, fathername, altmobno, yoa — as headings, with no display labels, no formatting, no column hiding and no reordering. Any schema change immediately and silently changes the user-facing report, and the code's one use of a column name, Cells("rollno"), couples the mutation paths to that physical name.
rules.complexity_rationale: Driven by what the Designer omits plus two runtime property assignments; the coupling it creates matters more than its logic.

conditions.condition: The grid is bound to a DataTable

actions.action: Generate one column per result-set field, in result-set order, titled with the raw column name
Distribute column widths to fill the available area

test_hints.happy_path: Ten columns appear with their database names as headers and widths filling the grid.
error_paths: Renaming or dropping the rollno column breaks Cells('rollno') at runtime with a column-not-found exception
boundary_conditions: Date of birth and mobile numbers are rendered with default type formatting, so dates display in workstation locale format and mobile numbers display as plain integers without leading zeros
Adding a column to the table silently adds it to the user-visible report, including any column holding sensitive data

rules.name: Reused edit form accumulates duplicate close handlers
rules.description: The Update handler attaches a FormClosed handler to the edit form on every click, but only constructs a new edit form when none exists or the previous one was disposed; otherwise it reuses the instance via UpdateRollNo. Because AddHandler is unconditional while construction is not, each reuse adds another subscription to the same event on the same instance. The grid reload therefore runs once on the first edit, twice on the second, three times on the third, and so on, producing N redundant full-table queries and rebinds per close.
rules.complexity_rationale: An asymmetry between a conditional construction and an unconditional subscription, whose effect accumulates across the session and is invisible at any single call site.

conditions.condition: An existing non-disposed edit form instance is reused for another record
AddHandler runs again on the same instance

actions.action: Register an additional FormClosed subscription without removing the previous one
On close, run the grid reload once per accumulated subscription

test_hints.happy_path: Edit one record and close it — the grid reloads exactly once.
error_paths: No visible error; the symptom is escalating redundant database work and grid flicker across a long session
boundary_conditions: Because EditForm.btnSave_Click calls Me.Close(), the form is disposed after each save and the next click constructs a fresh instance — so the accumulation only occurs along the Cancel path, where Close also disposes it. The reuse branch via UpdateRollNo is therefore rarely reached in practice, making this a latent rather than an everyday defect, and the dead reuse branch is itself a maintenance hazard.

rules.name: Editing is launched from the grid into the dashboard's host panel
rules.description: The Update handler does not open a dialog: it constructs the edit form, sets TopLevel to False and adds it to Form1's Panel5 through the Form1 default instance, reaching across module boundaries into the dashboard's control tree. The edit form is therefore a sibling of the view form inside the same host panel rather than a child of it, and the view form remains live and bound underneath.
rules.complexity_rationale: A child module mutates the parent shell's control collection via a default instance, inverting the expected ownership direction and coupling view-form to form1-dashboard's internal layout.

conditions.condition: A row is selected and Update is clicked

actions.action: Construct the edit form for the selected roll number
Reparent it into Form1.Panel5 via the Form1 default instance and bring it to front

test_hints.happy_path: Select a row, click Update, and the edit form appears over the dashboard's content panel.
error_paths: Any load failure crashes unhandled because this handler has no Try/Catch (BR-035)
boundary_conditions: The view form stays visible behind the edit form and its stale grid is still interactable
Panel5 accumulates child form controls that are hidden rather than removed (BR-078)

rules.name: Gender census counts only Male and Female
rules.description: The dashboard's gender breakdown runs exactly two COUNT queries, for gender = 'Male' and gender = 'Female'. The data-entry forms, however, offer three permitted values including 'Other' (BR-013). A student recorded as Other is storable, listable and editable but is counted in no gender statistic and in no total, so the two gender tiles do not sum to the student population and there is no tile, label or total anywhere on the dashboard that would reveal the shortfall. The enumeration is enforced in two files and contradicted by the single place that aggregates it.
rules.complexity_rationale: Two independent queries whose correctness depends on a value set defined in two other files; the defect is a silent undercount with no reconciling total.

conditions.condition: Dashboard statistics are loaded
One or more students are recorded with gender 'Other'

actions.action: Count rows where gender = 'Male' and display in the Male tile
Count rows where gender = 'Female' and display in the Female tile
Students recorded as Other are counted nowhere

test_hints.happy_path: With only Male and Female students recorded, the two tiles sum to the full population.
error_paths: Provider failure on either query raises an unhandled exception inside Form_Load (BR-076)
boundary_conditions: A single student recorded as Other makes the gender tiles under-report the population with no visible indication

rules.name: All dashboard statistics are whole-table and all-time
rules.description: Every one of the twelve dashboard counts queries the entire students table with no scoping predicate other than the single attribute it breaks down by. Because deletion is physical (BR-057), a student who leaves is removed rather than marked inactive, so 'all-time' and 'currently enrolled' are the same number by construction and the dashboard cannot distinguish them.

rules.name: No authentication or authorization of any kind
rules.description: The application has no login, no user identity, no roles, no permissions and no audit of actor. Authentication mode is set to Windows in the application framework configuration, but that only governs the My.User object, which the code never reads: no code path anywhere tests identity, group membership or privilege. Anyone able to launch the executable and reach the Access file has unrestricted create, read, update and delete authority over every student record, including the personal data of students and of named parents. The Access database itself has no database password and Jet workgroup security is unused. The only gate in front of a destructive operation is the row-selection test and the delete confirmation dialog.
rules.complexity_rationale: The rule is a complete absence of logic, which is precisely why it must be recorded explicitly: a modernization target that assumes authorization exists somewhere in this code will find nothing to port.

Several of the application's most significant data-integrity rules exist only because this switch is off.

rules.description: The project sets Option Compare Binary, so all VB string comparison in application code is case-sensitive and ordinal. The Access engine, by contrast, compares text case-insensitively. The same conceptual equality therefore has two different answers depending on which side evaluates it: the dropdown repopulation on the edit form matches stored values case-sensitively in .NET and silently fails on a case difference (BR-033), while the dashboard's gender and course counts and the search's roll-number equality all match case-insensitively in SQL. Any logic moved between the two layers during modernization changes behaviour.
rules.complexity_rationale: A build setting whose divergence from the data engine's semantics is invisible in source and changes the meaning of equality depending on evaluation site.

rules.name: No transactions anywhere
rules.description: No code path begins, commits or rolls back a transaction. Every mutation is a single autocommitted statement, which is sufficient for the current single-statement operations but means there is no atomicity between a mutation and its dependent side effects: the insert path commits a row and then performs refresh work that can itself fail and report an error for an operation that actually succeeded, and a delete-and-recreate re-key loses the record irrecoverably if interrupted in between.
rules.complexity_rationale: Defined by uniform absence; it fixes the atomicity guarantee of the whole system at single-statement granularity.

rules.name: Concurrent instances are permitted with last-write-wins
rules.description: Single-instance mode is explicitly disabled, so any number of copies can run against the same Access file, each with its own shared connection. There is no optimistic concurrency token, no row version, no timestamp and no change detection: the update writes all nine fields unconditionally, so the last save wins silently and the loser's edits are destroyed with no warning to either user. Refresh is navigation-driven only, so each instance shows data that may be arbitrarily stale. File-level locking is handled by the Access engine through the lock file, which serialises writes but provides no application-level conflict detection.
rules.complexity_rationale: An application-framework setting combined with the absence of any concurrency control, producing silent data loss across two modules and the data layer.

rules.name: No record provenance, audit trail or lifecycle state
rules.description: The students table has exactly ten business columns and no created-at, created-by, modified-at, modified-by, version or status column, and the application writes no audit record for any operation. It is therefore impossible to establish when a student record was created or last changed, who changed it, what the previous values were, or whether a student is current, graduated or withdrawn. Combined with physical deletion and the absence of any actor identity, no create, update or delete in this system is attributable or reconstructible after the fact — a material constraint on any modernization that must demonstrate data lineage or support data-subject requests over this personal data.
rules.complexity_rationale: Defined by schema and code omission across every module; no logic, but it bounds what any downstream compliance or reporting requirement can possibly be satisfied from.
